# develop's required status-check contexts, as read from
# GET /repos/digithings-ai/digithings/branches/develop/protection
#
# This is the guard's input. It is a committed snapshot, not a live read,
# because `administration: read` — which the branch-protection endpoint needs —
# cannot be granted to GITHUB_TOKEN at all, so no workflow can read it.
#
# KEEPING IT TRUE
#
# Every line here is a name GitHub will wait for forever if the producing
# workflow ever stops reporting. So before changing branch protection by hand:
#
#   python3 scripts/enable_branch_protection.py status \
#       --repo digithings-ai/digithings --branch develop
#
# and then re-run the guard, which is the same read the human runbook does:
#
#   python3 scripts/check_required_policy_checks.py --live \
#       --repo digithings-ai/digithings --branch develop
#
# `scripts/set-branch-protection.sh` writes protection; edit this file in the
# same change. `scripts/check_required_policy_checks.py` fails if the two drift.
#
# The `--live` read above is also on a clock: the unnamed `policy-gate-live`
# job in ci-pr-hygiene.yml runs it daily via the digithings-cron dispatch and
# fails when this file disagrees with the live gate, so a hand edit that forgot
# to update the snapshot becomes a dated red run rather than invisible drift.
# It can never gate a merge — see docs/ops/policy-check-credential.md — and an
# absent credential makes it report *unvalidated*, not fail. See
# docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md § Re-verifying the snapshot on a clock.
